pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care & Enrichment Opportunities
At Siddington C of E, we understand the importance of providing high-quality wraparound care that supports busy families while enriching every child’s school experience. Our before and after school care is a safe, nurturing environment where children can relax, learn, and grow outside of regular school hours.
At Siddington, every voice is valued.
I have been fortunate enough to be a volunteer at Siddington School for the past 15 months and wanted to express the delight that I feel each day that I go into each class. There is a kindness that is apparent in every teacher and class and ultimately, so strongly in each child.Volunteer reader
At Siddington, we are Responsible.
We are a small, rural Church of England school that sits on tranquil grounds. We have a large area dedicated to Forest School where the children experience a holistic education lead by our very own qualified FS teacher.

Welcome to SiddingtonC of E Primary School
Welcome to Siddington C of E Primary School, a small school situated in a rural village in Gloucestershire. Our motto, which we weave through school life is to be ‘responsible, kind and safe’. We recognise that a child’s journey through primary school has the opportunity to shape a future. We aspire for every child to feel nurtured, cared for and valued so that they may become aspirational learners with enquiring minds and deeply held values, ready to take on their responsibilities as global citizens.
To find out more about our school, please don’t hesitate to book a tour with Mrs R. Achary in the school office.

pageCache.pageTitle: British Values - Siddington C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
British Values
Promoting Fundamental British Values
In accordance with The Department for Education we aim to actively promote British values in schools to ensure young people leave school prepared for life in modern Britain. Pupils are encouraged to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance and understand that while different people may hold different views about what is ‘right’ and ‘wrong’, all people living in England are subject to its law.
The Key Values are:
democracy
rule of law
individual liberty
mutual respect
tolerance of those of different faiths and beliefs

Creativity
Our Vision
“I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made,” Psalm 139:14
At Siddington we create a culture of belonging where pupils are nurtured, appreciated and enabled to flourish. We want all pupils to develop uniquely and become the best version of themselves; each individual voice is valued.
Our school family will welcome our diverse community, embracing our unique location and the varied industries and skills we have right on our doorstep. We aim to build trust and meaningful connections with all.
Through our engaging and knowledge-rich curriculum, driven by our Christian values, we will set high expectations and challenge our pupils. We will foster self-belief and create the balance between emotional well-being and the highest rates of academic achievement. Our compassionate pupils will value school and know it is for them.
Learning at Siddington will inspire creative-thinkers, courageous individuals and responsible members of a global society.
TrustResponsibilityCompassion Hope Courage Creativity

Why is creativity important to us?
A lot of our teaching starts from well-written books that inspire creative-thinkers. When our pupils are faced with a problem, we teach them to look at in different ways and then investigate ways to solve it creatively. This could be a problem in mathematics, an issue with a friendship or even a global dilemma. We encourage individuality, pupils knowing that their voice is valued.

Enabling the language of spirituality, is experiencing something which is beyond words. As a Church of England School, we have a shared language of spirituality that we tac our children to use. This language begins from the Christian understanding that everyone is a valued creation, individually and uniquely made by God, like pots made by a potter (Isaiah 64:8). Yet in life things happen that impact on the physical ‘pot’ of life and create cracks that provide a glimpse of ‘something’ beyond the tangible. Christians would view this as an opportunity to relate to the Divine Creator God.
Kintsugi, the Japanese art of mending broken ceramics with golden joinery, makes something broken into something differently beautiful and even more valuable. Using this metaphor, the OWS, WOWS and NOWS of life offer the possibility of becoming cracks that are filled with gold, adding significance and value to life.Diocese of Gloucester

Why is responsibility important to us?
We want our pupils to become responsible members of a global society. We teach them to have a sense of responsibility for themselves, others and their environment – from the classroom to the wider world. We have high expectations of all of pupils to behave in a responsible, kind and safe way. You will see our pupils being responsible for their learning in class by listening well, asking questions to further their understanding and responding to questions thoughtfully. Recently, we have had a Be Responsible Friday where pupils, teachers and families have been invited to look after our school grounds: gardening, sweeping, painting and jet washing litter picking. It was a great success! Pupils feedback was positive and they said that they would like this opportunity more often.

SEND Vision
SEND Information and Offer
The school Special Educational Needs and Disability Coordinator is Miss Briony Smith.Her email: sendco@siddington.gloucs.sch.uk
Date of creation
No options...
Our Core Offer
This offer is common to schools within the South Cotswold Schools Partnership.
Siddington C of E Primary School values the contribution that every child can make and is supported by the Local Authority to ensure that all pupils, regardless of their specific needs, make the best possible progress. The school seeks to raise the achievement, remove barriers to learning and increase physical and curricular access to all. All children and young people with Special Educational Needs or Disabilities (SEND) are valued, respected and considered equal members of the school. As such, provision for pupils with SEND is a matter for the school as a whole. All teachers are teachers of pupils with SEND. The Governing Body, Headteacher, SENDCO and all other members of staff are responsible for teaching children with SEND. This local offer is in line with the school SEND policy which can be accessed via the website or by contacting the school office.
Who are the best people to talk to in this school about my child’s difficulties with learning/Special Educational Needs or Disability?
The SENDCo is Mrs Briony Smith.

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher Welcome Message - Siddington C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher Welcome Message
Welcome to Siddington C of E Primary School, a small school situated in a unique location between a rural village and a busy industrial estate. Our school family welcomes our diverse community, embraces our unique location and the varied industries and skills we have right on our doorstep. On one walking route to school, you will pass paddocks with grazing sheep and goats. In the spring, you can hear them bleat whilst they play in the surrounding fields. Our school has large grounds. You will find: a sports pitch, a trike track, a climbing frame, an outdoor gym, a Reflection Garden, an allotment, a large field, a running track and an extensive space dedicated to Forest School. There are zoned areas where children can be creative, develop resilience and learn how to respect nature. All pupils have the opportunity to experience outdoor learning and are taught by our very own qualified Forest School teacher.
In Physical Education, children are coached by a specialist and have opportunities to participate with competitive events at local schools. As the school grows, we are making links with local artists, businesses and charities who will join us in our journey to put our school on the map.
Our intake into Reception is fifteen pupils. In Reception, they will start their journey as a Robin and be taught in a small class of up to 15 pupils with a class teacher and a teaching assistant. We then have mixed-age year groups.
Our school Christian values are standards of behaviour that we believe enable us all to flourish. These values are evident in Psalm 139 – “I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made,” Psalm 139:14. At Siddington we create a culture of belonging where pupils are nurtured, appreciated and enabled to flourish. We want all pupils to develop uniquely and become the best version of themselves; each individual voice is valued.
Mrs Rachael ScottHeadteacher

Why is compassion important to us?
We have three simple rules: be responsible, be kind and be safe. Our pupils are taught that compassion is caring about themselves, others and the world around them. They learn about different emotions and how we can recognise them in ourselves and others. We teach them to be kind by identifying what kindness looks like, sounds like and feels like.
‘The Lord is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger in rich in love. The Lord is good to all; he has compassion on all he has made.’ Psalm 145: 8-9

5 You are all around me—in front and in back.You have put your hand on me.
6 Your knowledge is amazing to me. It is more than I can understand.
Psalm 139 – God knows everything

Why is courage important to us?
We want our pupils to be courageous individuals who develop uniquely and know how to be the best version of themselves. We strive for them to have high expectations and accept challenges with a positive mindset.
We teach the rewarding benefits of being persevering and having resilience through the Japanese proverb:
“Nana korobi ya oki” which translated means ‘Fall down seven times, get up eight’. The proverb speaks to the Japanese concept of resilience and the ‘insistence’ that no matter how many times you get knocked down, you must get up again.

Learning at Siddington will inspire creative-thinkers, courageous individuals and responsible members of a global society.

Why is trust important to us?
To create a true sense of belonging, we must all feel valued and trusted. If we want to understand each other, we need to listen and learn from each other. We must be prepared to be challenged by our friends, our peers and our teachers and we must be ready to work together for the common good. Building relationships of trust and mutual respect is crucial. Learning about each others’ beliefs – what we treasure and what inspires us – helps us get to know one another. Having trustworthy relationships means we can share what is unique about us and help us disagree well on those things where we fundamentally differ.

OW, WOW, NOW
Enabling the language of spirituality, is experiencing something which is beyond words. As a Church of England School, we have a shared language of spirituality that we tac our children to use. This language begins from the Christian understanding that everyone is a valued creation, individually and uniquely made by God, like pots made by a potter (Isaiah 64:8). Yet in life things happen that impact on the physical ‘pot’ of life and create cracks that provide a glimpse of ‘something’ beyond the tangible. Christians would view this as an opportunity to relate to the Divine Creator God.
Kintsugi, the Japanese art of mending broken ceramics with golden joinery, makes something broken into something differently beautiful and even more valuable. Using this metaphor, the OWS, WOWS and NOWS of life offer the possibility of becoming cracks that are filled with gold, adding significance and value to life.

pageCache.text:
Headteacher Welcome Message
Welcome to Siddington C of E Primary School, a small school situated in a unique location between a rural village and a busy industrial estate. Our school family welcomes our diverse community, embraces our unique location and the varied industries and skills we have right on our doorstep. On one walking route to school, you will pass paddocks with grazing sheep and goats. In the spring, you can hear them bleat whilst they play in the surrounding fields. Our school has large grounds. You will find: a sports pitch, a trike track, a climbing frame, an outdoor gym, a Reflection Garden, an allotment, a large field, a running track and an extensive space dedicated to Forest School. There are zoned areas where children can be creative, develop resilience and learn how to respect nature. All pupils have the opportunity to experience outdoor learning and are taught by our very own qualified Forest School teacher.
In Physical Education, children are coached by a specialist and have opportunities to participate with competitive events at local schools. As the school grows, we are making links with local artists, businesses and charities who will join us in our journey to put our school on the map.
Our intake into Reception is fifteen pupils. In Reception, they will start their journey as a Robin and be taught in a small class of up to 15 pupils with a class teacher and a teaching assistant. We then have mixed-age year groups.
Our school Christian values are standards of behaviour that we believe enable us all to flourish. These values are evident in Psalm 139 – “I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made,” Psalm 139:14. At Siddington we create a culture of belonging where pupils are nurtured, appreciated and enabled to flourish. We want all pupils to develop uniquely and become the best version of themselves; each individual voice is valued.
Mrs Rachael ScottHeadteacher

The office will then manually credit your ParentPay account as requested. This will then enable you to make bookings. The only further action required from you is that you monitor your ParentPay account to check that there is enough credit in the account to cover costs at all times.

Governors
The role of the Local Governing Body is to provide focused governance for the school at a local level. We monitor the school’s key performance indicators and act as a critical friend to the Head Teacher, providing challenge where appropriate. We also play a part in representing the views of all the school stakeholders: children, staff and parents; as well as offering assistance to the Academy Trustees in the fulfillment of their duties.
Please find below details of how our Governing body is structured, including the names, categories, responsibilities and terms of appointment for each Governor.
